teams.heading: Matt Dawson says England must embrace favourites tag before All Blacks clash
teams.body: Writing after England's 78-15 demolition of Japan, BBC Sport columnist and England World Cup winner Matt Dawson wants England head coach Steve Borthwick's side bombarded with the favourites tag before Saturday's clash with New Zealand. He believes they are favourites, pointing to Wales' 35-28 win over the All Blacks as the reason he has faith in this group. Having beaten New Zealand last year, Dawson says England should not approach this home fixture with an underdog mentality.

teams.heading: Grégory Alldritt returns at No. 8 against South Africa, with doubts unresolved
teams.body: Grégory Alldritt started at No. 8 in Friday's 21-19 win over South Africa at the Stade de France, his first Bleus appearance in a year. He made 12 carries for 31 metres, beat a defender, had a clean sheet on his aerial catches and was involved in 22 ruck situations. Doubts about sustaining his intensity remain, but in his duel with Springbok Jasper Wiese the Stade Rochelais captain posted the better output over near-identical minutes, 49 to 45.

lead.why: A fresh France story about Alldritt's first Bleus appearance in a year, with a new analysis piece that the pack reports today.

teams.heading: Sam Prendergast cited over Fiji hip-drop tackle, risking Springboks test absence
teams.body: Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast was cited after the 43-15 win over Fiji for a hip-drop tackle on captain Peceli Yato in the first half, an incident that went unpunished on the day. The 23-year-old now faces a disciplinary process that could keep him out of the South Africa game in Dublin. Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus says the tackle should have been a red card, yet he expects Prendergast to play: "I think there is going to be a technicality and he is going to play."

lead.why: A fresh disciplinary event involving an Ireland starter, with a direct bearing on availability for the South Africa test.

teams.heading: Quesada's Italy to name Fiji side by press release on Thursday
teams.body: Italy's Fiji build-up is laid out in the federation's media programme. Head coach Gonzalo Quesada's squad will be announced by press release on Thursday, with a Zoom press conference the same day, and the captain's run is set for Friday at Udine's Bluenergy Stadium, the first 15 minutes open to media. The Fiji match is the third of Italy's November window, after the 7-66 loss to South Africa and the 14-19 defeat by Argentina in Genoa. The federation says timings may shift with the squad's commitments.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item on the shortlist, and it sets out when Italy's Fiji team will be named and how the build-up runs.

teams.heading: Gregor Townsend hails Scotland's defence after 15-12 'arm wrestle' win over Australia
teams.body: Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend said his side's defence was "one of the best performances I've seen in the last couple of years", in a Nations Championship "arm wrestle" that never produced the bonus point. The win followed a defeat by New Zealand in which Scotland failed to score a second-half point. Max Jorgensen's late converted try had given the Wallabies hope before Darcy Graham's superb tackle hauled full-back Tom Wright into touch as the clock ran red.

teams.heading: James Botham named man of the match as Wales beat All Blacks
teams.body: Wales blindside flanker James Botham was named man of the match in the 35-28 win over New Zealand, a first victory over the All Blacks in 73 years. Once play resumed he was everywhere, tackling, scrambling and springing back up. His Wales debut came against Georgia in November 2020 at an empty Parc y Scarlets, and injuries and competition later kept him out of the side for more than two and a half years. Former Wales and Lions captain Sam Warburton, who has watched him since he first came to Cardiff, rates his footwork for contact.

lead.why: A fresh, player-centred post-match story about Wales's man of the match, which the pack reports today and which is not a retelling of the Roberts or Cuthbert pieces.

teams.heading: Sclavi and Elías yellow cards: Pumas hold on to beat Italy
teams.body: Joel Sclavi and Efraín Elías were both shown yellow cards three minutes apart in the final quarter, leaving the Pumas playing with thirteen for an extended spell. Elías's card also handed Italy a penalty try, and Argentina had to dig deep to hold on. Pablo Matera kept his players relatively calm while Italy pressed for a comeback. The 19-14 win was the second of the 2026 Nations Championship.

teams.heading: Les Kiss' Wallabies lost the collisions that mattered at Murrayfield, Gallan argues
teams.body: Gallan's Guardian analysis of the 15-12 loss points to the gainline as the core failure. One lineout sequence near Scotland's 22 around the 66th minute shows it: after nine phases Australia had gone roughly five metres backwards, and after 18 phases the move ended with a turnover by Rory Darge. Kiss had already flagged the problem after the England defeat, saying, "We gave them too much at the gainline for sure."

teams.heading: Warner Dearns, who left New Zealand aged 14, co-captained Japan at Twickenham
teams.body: The second row's route to Saturday's Twickenham captaincy began with a reluctant move: his father Grant took a strength and conditioning job with NEC Green Rockets, and 14-year-old Dearns said he did not want to leave New Zealand. Having qualified on residency grounds, he debuted for Japan in November 2021 at 19 and featured in all four matches at the 2023 Rugby World Cup. This year he spent a season's sabbatical at the Hurricanes, helping Wellington to their first Super Rugby title in a decade.

lead.why: It is the freshest Japan angle in the pack, a new profile of co-captain Warner Dearns rather than another retelling of the defeat or the red card.

teams.heading: Taine Randell: Barrett, Mo'unga could have played final Tests after Wales loss
teams.body: Speaking on The Platform NZ podcast, former All Blacks captain Taine Randell said Beauden Barrett and Richie Mo'unga could have played their final Tests against Wales in Cardiff. Barrett started at full-back and captained New Zealand at Test level for the first time, while Mo'unga, in his 58th Test, wore the No. 10 jersey. Randell pointed to thin cover at first-five, with Ruben Love injured and four players who are all first-fives. He added that the younger players will get more chances.

lead.why: A fresh, New Zealand-specific item on Barrett and Mo'unga's futures after the Wales defeat, ranked above the older Wales and Rennie pieces.

teams.heading: Kolisi says France seized their chances as Springboks lose 19-21 in Paris
teams.body: Beaten in Paris for the first time in 21 years, the Springboks were gracious in defeat. Captain Siya Kolisi said France took the chances they created, while lock Ruan Nortjé credited France's players for fighting hard to protect their lead and said they fully deserved the win. Openside flank Paul de Villiers said the Boks created plenty but could not turn opportunities into points, a finishing problem they will study closely before Ireland.

lead.why: The highest-ranked new South Africa item, and a same-team post-match reaction from Kolisi, Nortjé and de Villiers after the 19-21 defeat to France.
